pr_body: As discussed with @mattdangerw, I am opening this PR to fix #16113 memory inefficiency in RNNs.
pr_comments:
Thanks for your pull request! It looks like this may be your first contribution to a Google open source project. Before we can look at your pull request, you'll need to sign a Contributor License Agreement (CLA).

For more information, open the [CLA check for this pull request](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/pull/16174/checks?check_run_id=5428810783).

@fchollet just saw the test log. I think it comes from the following: 
`LSTM` and `GRU` have different functions to execute in CPU and GPU (the other RNNs layers don't). CPU version calls `backend.rnn` (the function I updated), but GPU calls `tf.raw_ops.CudnnRNN`. I updated the CPU version to properly call the new version of `backend.rnn`, but the GPU one will always return `outputs` as `tf.raw_ops.CudnnRNN` always returns the full array.

The error happens in the tests that combine CPU and GPU environments.

I see three options to solve this:
1. Deactivate new functionality in `LSTM` and `GRU`. As mentioned in the original issue #16113, the layers most affected by the current behavior are convolutional RNNs, for which the update works perfectly.
2. Although `tf.raw_ops.CudnnRNN` returns `outputs`, the GPU method can still return `outputs=[last_output]`. The memory advantage will not be available in GPU for `LSTM` and `GRU`, but the return format from both CPU and GPU would be consistent.
3. Update `tf.raw_ops.CudnnRNN` in a similar way than `backend.rnn`. However, I have not been able to find the source code of that function in the [tensorflow repository](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow).

I think the ideal solution would be 3. For the time being, I would go for 2. Let me know what you think!

PS: I had executed the tests locally with no errors. I have re-executed them again and no errors were found, as can be seen in [this notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/atmguille/keras-pr-gpu-tests).
Let's do option 2.  Option 3. is not realistically doable given that the computation is delegated to cuDNN.

I believe it should be fixed now. I have executed all tests locally and there are no errors. However, there were no errors also before this fix, as I mentioned in my last comment. Let's see

Thanks again for your time @fchollet

@fchollet I saw how the tests you requested worked but the tests that have just executed do not.
 The log shows the following:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45051399/157515054-1af1b713-9ae9-47e2-9f5c-2213b954ad89.png)
Maybe floating point operations errors being not deterministic? That would explain why your tests passed and these do not. Should we try to run them again? Let me know how I can help

Edit: I have checked the code of the test that fails and apparently it has nothing to do with my updates. The model being tested is [this one](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/61edccb559c0daf243149c62a03f58c019db387d/keras/distribute/keras_image_model_correctness_test.py#L33)
I think this is possibly a case of flaky test. Let's try rerunning the tests.

The tests have passed! I am not sure if you need to approve my last review request, as the PR is "Approved by Reviewer" but it also shows that there is 1 pending reviewer.

Anyway, thanks a lot for your time! It was a good learning experience as my first contribution @fchollet

issue_context.title: Memory inefficiency in RNNs
issue_context.body:
**Context**
I have been working with small `ConvLSTM` architecture and getting an OOM with a moderate number of filters. I think I have detected a memory inefficiency related to RNNs that may be the root cause, although I have not been able to fully solve the problem.

**System information**.
TensorFlow version (you are using): 2.6.2
GPU model and memory: Tesla P100 16GB (Kaggle GPU)
Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): Yes

**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state**.
At the moment, `keras.backend.rnn` returns the tuple `(last_output, outputs, new_states)`. Layers that call this method may only require *last_output*, so retrieving and storing *outputs* in memory, in this case, is inefficient and not needed.

The current behavior is especially harmful to Convolutional versions of RNNs and LSTMs, since storing *outputs* means storing something close to n_filters * input. For example, if a `ConvLSTM` with 50 filters 3x3 is instantiated and is applied to a video with 100x100 frames, `keras.backend.rnn` will return 50 copies of the complete video (98x98 frames) even if `return_sequences=False`, when just the last 98x98 frame for each filter is needed. 

As it can be seen from the example, if the current state is as described, the memory impact can be huge, restricting the use of ConvLSTMs to a moderate number of filters even with simple architectures.

**Will this change the current api? How?**
Yes. `keras.backend.rnn` will receive a flag (*return_all_outputs*) indicating if all outputs from the process have to be returned, and thus kept in memory. If not, only last_output will be kept during the process, saving the corresponding memory.
To keep the current return format, if *return_all_outputs* is False, the method can still return the tuple `(last_output, [last_output], new_states)`.

**Who will benefit from this feature?**
The whole community, especially users using Convolutional versions of RNNs and LSTMs. Other users have reported similar memory issues with ConvLSTMs in StackOverflow (for instance: [link](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66859089/getting-oom-with-small-convlstm-model)).

**[Contributing](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)**

- Do you want to contribute a PR? (yes/no): yes
- If yes, please read [this page](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for instructions
- Briefly describe your candidate solution(if contributing): the solution described in the API Changes has been implemented in [this repo](https://github.com/atmguille/convlstm-saving-memory). Some TODOs are pending, like applying masks correctly to outputs when *return_all_outputs* is False. However, other updates are needed, since it does not solve the OOM of my original problem.

**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**.
Check [this notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/atmguille/convlstm-oom/notebook#ConvLSTM) to see how a simple architecture results in an OOM. Especially worrying is the following line of the provided logs: 
```
2022-02-23 00:08:53.579673: I tensorflow/core/common_runtime/bfc_allocator.cc:1011] Bin (16777216): 	Total Chunks: 826, Chunks in use: 826. 14.79GiB allocated for chunks. 14.79GiB in use in bin. 14.78GiB client-requested in use in bin.
```
Check [this notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/atmguille/convlstm-oom-using-proposal/notebook#Load-proposal-code) that imports my proposal, which also gets an OOM.

I have done some experiments in CPU and experienced better performance in RAM usage for small number of filters. However, as I mentioned in the issue, I may be missing something else for GPU.

Thanks for your time. Let me know what are the next steps!

Tagging @qlzh727 and @fchollet who probably know the most about Keras RNN layers to see if they have thoughts.

I would say next could be opening a pull request and we can continue discussion there.

review_comments: When `return_all_outputs=False` we don't need the TensorArray logic at all, right?

Totally agree @fchollet . I just wanted to change the logic as little as possible. By having a common TensorArray, the only things that change when `return_all_outputs=False` is the size and that we always write at index 0; similar to what I did in the `unroll=True` branch when keeping a list of one element.

Of course, suggestions are more than welcome to improve this :)
